 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE RAJIV ROY
ORAL ORDER 5 23-03-2023 Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, the State and the informant.

2.The present petition has been preferred for quashing of the order dated 05.08.2015 passed in G.R.
Case No. 3220/02 arising out of Pirbahore P.S. Case No. 300/02 dated 06.09.2002 by Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Patna under Sections 419 and 420 of the I.P.C. by which discharge petition filed under Section 239 of the Cr.P.C. has been rejected.

3. As per the allegation made by the Principal, Patna College, Patna University, Patna, it was alleged that in an examination no. 46/1998 conducted by the Bihar Public Service Commission (henceforth for short 'the BPSC') this petitioner Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.56054 of 2015(5)
dt.23-03-2023 was appearing on behalf of one Prem Kumar having Roll No. 193389 on 06.09.2002 in the general knowledge subject examination.

4. As upon interrogation by those who were present in the examination center within the campus of Patna College, he chose not to disclose his name, the Pirbahore Police was called upon and he was handed over to them.

sentences.text: 5. Accordingly, Pirbahore P.S. Case No. 300/2002 dated 06.09.2002 under Section 419 and 420 of the I.P.C. was lodged.

6. The police investigated the matter and as per the case diary, it came to the knowledge that the petitioner was staying at the house of Prem Kumar/his elder brother at 50A/1605 at Mahatma Gandhinagar, Kanti Factory Road near Budha Dental Hospital in the district of Patna and he confessed before the police that in lieu of money, he accepted the proposal for appearing on behalf of the said Prem Kumar.
7.
As per him, he had earlier also appeared in the said examination but on 06.09.2002, he was apprehended.

The petition of the petitioner fully supports the confession made by him as the present address in the petition clearly shows his place of residence at 50A/1605, Mahatma Gandhi Nagar, Kanti Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.56054 of 2015(5) dt.23-03-2023 Factory Road near Budha Dental Hospital, Patna which is also the residence of Prem Kumar.

8. As per the case diary, in paragraph 5, the re- statement of the Principal of Patna College, namely,
Rajendra Prasad Rahi has been recorded which follows the statement of P.K. Singh, PTI, Patna College, Patna, (a staff of the said college) as also one Suresh Prasad of Patna College and all of them have stated that the petitioner was appearing on 06.09.2002 in the General Knowledge examination in the Gymnasium Hall with the Roll No. 193389 which was allotted to one Prem Kumar.
9. Further, it was during the Magistrate checking that he was apprehended.
Suresh Prasad in his statement averred that on earlier occasion also they had detected him but on that date, he managed to get out of center but on 06.09.2002, he was finally apprehended.
10. Then, there are statement of the independent witness namely, Krishan Kumar as also another staff Ramashish Prasad "Daftari" who have also supported the prosecution story.
11. It is the case of the learned counsel for the petitioner that on 06.09.2002, no such examination had taken place and he has brought on record the admit card of said Prem Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.56054 of 2015(5) dt.23-03-2023 Kumar which although not readable shows a date as 04.09.2002.

12. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that provisional admit card issued to the Prem Kumar shows the examination program as follows:
(i) on 27.07.2002 Hindi (2 P.M.
-5P.M.);
(ii) on 28.07.2002 General Knowledge (10 A.M. -01 P.M.) and (iii) on 28.07.2002 Mathematics (2 P.M.-5P.M.)
Vishal Kumar @Cofi vs The State Of Bihar on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78453844/
2 13.

sentences.text: He as such submits that when the examination was in July, there was no occasion to appear and or get apprehended on 06.09.2002.
14. Upon query, whether any categorical statement has been made in the petition that no examination of General Knowledge took place on 06.09.2002, the answer of learned counsel is in negative.

15. The learned counsel for the petitioner further failed to provide any answer as to when he had nothing to do with Prem Kumar; how come his provisional admit card as also the attendance sheet came to his possession.
Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.56054 of 2015(5) dt.23-03-2023 16.
The next ground taken by the learned counsel for the petitioner is that there is no seizure list to show his complicity in the matter.

17. He submits that accordingly, when the police submitted charge-sheet under Section 419 and 420 of the I.P.C. and the learned Court took cognizance under the aforesaid section, he preferred discharge petition which came to be rejected on 05.08.2015.
18.
It is appropriate to bring on record the order dated 05.08.2015 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Civil Court, Patna in G.R. Case No. 3220/02.

sentences.text: "attendance has been filed by the accused person through their learned advocate Today this case record is fixed for order for petition of 239 of Cr.P.C.

Petition of Cr.P.C. was pressed by the learned counsel of accused Learned counsel states that the petitioner has not been named in the written report of the informant Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.56054 of 2015(5) dt.23-03-2023 and nothing has been recovered from the possession of the petitioner

He also states that there is no handwriting expert report in respect of writing available in any answer sheet and in absence of such documents there is no evidence to established as to who writes the answer sheet.
He also states that there is no evidence against accused person US. 419 and 420 of I.P.C.
Learned counsel prays for discharge of said petitioner U/S 239 of Cr.P.C..

Rejoinder petition 239 of Cr.P.C.
has been filed by the learned A.P.O.
The learned A.P.O, males that the petitioner is named accused in F.I.R. and in the C.D. several materials available against the said petitioner.

Learned A.P.O. also states that Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.56054 of 2015(5) dt.23-03-2023 charge sheet has been filed by 10.
against said petitioner after proper investigation.
Cognizance has been also taken against said petitioner.
Learned A.P.O. prays to reject above said petition.
Heard both of the parties.
Perused the case record and considering the materials available on the record this court finds that the petitioner is named accused person in FIR.

From perusal of the case record it also appears that cognizance has been also taken by the court of learned C.J.M. US. 419 and 420 of I.P.C. Where these alleged section are Vishal Kumar @Cofi vs The State Of Bihar on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78453844/
